source_views.source: Muhurta Chintamani of Rama Daivajna (with Hindi commentary; Source Library AI translation, unreviewed), ch. 1 v.42-43 (p.34)
source_views.view: Vishti is also called Bhadra; it falls in the first half of Shukla 8 and 15, second half of Shukla 4 and 11, second half of Krishna 3 and 10, and first half of Krishna 7 and 14. A major defect to be avoided for auspicious ceremonies; some hold its fault lasts only till midday.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra (English tr., archive.org 'ParasharaHoraSastra' text; chapter numbers as in that edition), ch. 85 sl. 1-4; ch. 88 sl. 1-5
source_views.view: Birth in Bhadra (Vishti) karana is listed among inauspicious births; remedy: Vishnu puja, ghee lamp and abhisheka at a Shiva temple, 108 rounds of a pipal tree, havan, feeding Brahmins, on the day Bhadra recurs.

disagreements: All sources read treat Vishti as unfavourable; Jataka Bharanam adds that the native nevertheless succeeds in undertakings, and Brihat Samhita that harsh acts (e.g. against enemies) succeed in it.
phrasing_guidance: Karana is a minor factor; one short line at most. Present Vishti (Bhadra) birth as a traditional caution with a devotional remedy; never call the person cruel or harmful.

remedies.remedy: Vishnu puja, ghee lamp and abhisheka at a Shiva temple, 108 rounds of a pipal tree, havan, feeding Brahmins, on the day Bhadra recurs
